title: A Hummingbird's Heart Beats 1,260 Times a Minute. Then It Nearly Stops

scenes.text: A hummingbird's heart beats 1,260 times a minute.
That's 21 beats every second. Yours does about one.
Its wings beat 70 times a second just to hover. It has to eat all day, or starve.
So at night, it does something drastic. The heart drops to 50. Body temperature falls from 107 degrees to 48.
It goes stiff and cold, almost dead. Torpor. It saves just enough energy to last the night.
Then the sun comes up, and the heart kicks back to 1,260.

description:
A hummingbird's heart can race at up to 1,260 beats per minute in flight, and its wings beat around 70 times a second just to hover.
To survive the night without eating, it drops into torpor: the heart slows to as low as 50 beats a minute and body temperature can fall from about 107 degrees Fahrenheit to 48, so the bird sits cold and stiff until sunrise.
Would you trade sleep for a nightly shutdown like this? Comment below.
first_comment: Bonus: the bee hummingbird of Cuba weighs under two grams, less than a penny. Which animal do you think has the slowest heartbeat? (Hint: we covered one.)
